test_title: PYST 08: SSC Stenographer 2025: English Language & Comprehension (Held On: 08 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct direct speech form of the following sentence.

Sobhit said that he could speak more fluently than Rahul.

options.text: Sobhit said, "I can speak most fluently than Rahul."
Sobhit said, "I can speak more fluentlier than Rahul."
Sobhit said, "I can speak more fluently than Rahul."
Sobhit said, "I can spoke more fluently than Rahul."

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** Sobhit said that he could speak more fluently than Rahul.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **"he could speak" becomes "I can speak"**
 
 
• Pronoun "he" changes to "I" in direct speech.
 
• Verb "could" is converted to "can" to match the present tense of direct speech.
 
 
 
• **"more fluently than Rahul" remains unchanged.**
 
 
• The comparison and structure remain the same.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Format:**
 
 
• Direct speech is enclosed in quotation marks.
 
• Starts with a capital letter "I" and ends with a period "."
 
• Reporting clause precedes the quoted speech.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I can speak more fluently than Rahul," said Sobhit.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "I can speak most fluently than Rahul," said Sobhit.

 
 
• Incorrect comparative form "most fluently" used instead of "more fluently."
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "I can speak more fluentlier than Rahul," said Sobhit.
 
 
• Incorrect word "fluentlier" used; "fluently" is the correct form.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** "I can spoke more fluently than Rahul," said Sobhit.
 
 
• Incorrect verb tense "spoke" used; "can speak" is correct.
